subject: ACME POC — evaluation plan & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC — evaluation plan & next steps

Jamie — thanks again for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum on the POC: 

TL;DR: we propose a 4-week POC focused on the search-assist workflow you showed. Success = 20% reduction in avg time-to-resolution on sampled queries + no >5% regression in accuracy/precision on your high-value intents.

Proposed evaluation plan (high level):
- Duration: 4 weeks (pilot traffic window + offline evals)
- Success criteria: 
  - Metric A (TTR): >=20% reduction in average time-to-resolution on sampled production queries
  - Metric B (Precision@1 for high-value intents): within -5% of current baseline
  - Latency: 95th perc latency < 800ms for 95% of requests during pilot window
- Ownership:
  - Acme: provide sample query set, baseline metrics, and one sandbox account for shadowing (Ravi to provision)
  - Redwood: deliver model variants, quantization profile, batch config, and run offline evals + live shadow for 1 week
- Evaluation methodology:
  - Offline: curated holdout set + graded rubric (relevance, safety, hallucination, formatting)
  - Online: 1-week shadow run on non-customer-facing traffic to measure latency and throughput and to compute online proxies for quality
- Deliverables: weekly status updates, final eval report (metrics + sample outputs), and a recommended model/config for production

Next steps (action items):
1) Jamie / Ravi: share sample query set and baseline metrics by EOD Wed (2027-03-17) — required to scope offline evals.
2) Acme: create sandbox API key or provide limited access for shadowing (Ravi).
3) Redwood: Marissa will share an evaluation matrix + initial grading rubric by tomorrow.
4) Schedule kickoff: propose 2027-03-19 for a 30-min kickoff to align on data access and timeline.

Attachments: acme_poc_eval_matrix.xlsx (initial template)

Happy to adjust — fyi Marissa will follow up with the rubric & timeline.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acme.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — evaluation plan & next steps

Thanks, Dylan — that plan looks sensible. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Timeline: 4 weeks is fine but we need the offline evals completed in week 1 so our data-science team can review outputs in week 2. Can Redwood prioritize offline grading early?

2) Data/Privacy: We can provide a de-identified sample query set (~5k queries) and baseline KPIs by Wed EOD. For shadowing, we prefer the "online shadow" approach (no user-facing changes) and we can route a small percentage (~2%) of internal helpdesk traffic to the sandbox. We will not allow sending PII to external model endpoints — any logs we share must be pre-filtered.

3) Grading rubric: Our DS wants a simple 5-point relevance scale plus flags for hallucination and safety issues. Precision/recall numbers are useful but please include a human review component (10–20% of outputs).

4) Ownership: Ravi will provision the sandbox by Thu. He'll also loop in security if we need a short SCC (they prefer a standard questionnaire).

Can Marissa share the rubric and the matrix now so our team can review before kickoff?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Jamie
Head of Product | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC — evaluation plan & next steps

Jamie — great notes. Attached is a first-pass rubric (redwood_eval_rubric_v1.pdf) and an updated evaluation matrix (attached spreadsheet) — TL;DR below.

Offline vs Online (recommended approach):
- Week 1: Offline grading on de-identified sample (5k queries). Purpose: validate relevance & safety at scale and tune beam/temperature/stop settings. We’ll run model variants across your holdout set and return per-case scores + human-annotator flags.
- Week 2: Human review of sampled outputs (10–20% of worst/borderline cases) to calibrate the rubric and confirm failure modes.
- Week 3: Online shadow (2% internal traffic) to capture latency/throughput and surface unseen long-tail cases. No live routing to customers.
- Week 4: Final report + recommended config and runbook for rollout.

Rubric (summary):
- Relevance (1–5): 1 = irrelevant / unsafe, 5 = highly relevant and actionable
- Hallucination (Y/N + severity 1–3): mark when the model invents unsupported facts
- Safety/Policy Violation (Y/N): immediate fail if present
- Formatting/Actionability (1–3): is the response actionable without heavy post-processing
- Overall Pass/Fail: Pass if Relevance >=4 AND Hallucination = N AND Safety = N

Scoring & thresholds we propose to start with (tunable):
- Pass rate target: >=70% on the holdout for a go/no-go
- Precision@1 for high-value intents: within -5% of baseline (as Dylan wrote)

Practical notes:
- We will provide a CSV with per-query scores, grader notes, and sample outputs.
- For human graders we recommend your product SMEs + 2 Redwood annotators to minimize bias.
- We will not require full production data — de-identified queries are sufficient for offline grading. For the shadow run we’ll accept a copy of internal traffic that has been filtered for PII.

Next actions we’ll take today:
- Share the rubric PDF + updated matrix (attached).
- Prepare the offline grading job; will need your sample set by EOD Wed.

If the rubric looks good to you, we’ll proceed with offline grading on Thursday morning and target the kickoff on Fri 2027-03-19 at 10:00am PT.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_eval_rubric_v1.pdf, acme_poc_eval_matrix.xlsx
